# Risk memo: Classic 60/40

_Written by openai/gpt-oss-120b (openai). Verified: 0 unsupported numbers, 29 figures traced to code._

## Summary

The Classic 60/40 aims for balanced growth with a mix of equities and bonds. Over the analysis window it delivered a compound annual growth rate of 10.26% while the benchmark posted 15.58%.

## Return and risk profile

Annualized volatility was 11.01%, giving a Sharpe ratio of 0.67 and a Sortino ratio of 1.34. The maximum drawdown reached -22.20% over a period of 547 trading days, with the peak occurring on 2021-12-27 and the trough on 2022-10-14. The portfolio’s beta to the benchmark was 0.58, and its skewness and excess kurtosis were -0.17 and 11.88 respectively, indicating modest asymmetry and fat tails.

## Tail risk

One‑day 95 % historical VaR was 1.01% and the corresponding expected shortfall was 1.64%. The 99 % historical VaR stood at 1.92% with an expected shortfall of 2.85%. The Kupiec back‑test flagged the 95 % VaR as under‑estimating risk, while the 99 % VaR was consistent with observations. Monte‑Carlo simulation suggests a probability of loss over the next year of 32.05% and a chance of a drawdown worse than twenty percent of value of 5.10%.

## Stress and regimes

In the most severe historical stress scenario, the Global Financial Crisis, the portfolio lost -26.34% while the benchmark fell -46.04%. Other stress events produced losses of -10.60%, -18.81% and -21.49% respectively. The hidden Markov model identifies the current regime as Calm with a probability of 90.37%, and volatility in stress regimes is expected to be 6.4x times higher than in calm periods. The best forecast model for near‑term volatility is GARCH-t, which predicts an annualized volatility of 7.31% for the next month.

## Disclosed risks from filings

No 10-K filings are indexed for these holdings (ETFs and funds do not file them).

## Caveats and limitations

All figures are based on historical data and model assumptions; actual future performance may differ.

- All figures are historical estimates from daily data between 2016-11-01 and 2026-10-29; future losses can be larger.
- Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall assume the past is representative of the future; the normal-distribution versions understate fat tails.
- Monte Carlo results depend on the assumed annual return of 5.00% and resample past daily returns.
- Regimes come from a hidden Markov model fitted to the benchmark; the current regime uses only data up to the last date.
- Disclosed risks summarize the latest 10-K risk factors; ETFs and funds have none.
- The prose was written by a language model. Every figure was inserted by code from computed results and checked by an automatic verifier.

_Educational tool, not investment advice. Models are simplifications; historical risk measures can understate future losses._
